description:
Goal

Finish the callable-boundary architecture established by fz-k22.23. One producer-owned callable construction carries its correlated members behind one public callable boundary. Exact executable calls use DirectCallTarget::Local; first-class callable values are invoked indirectly through their public boundary. Native codegen must not retain a second per-FnId closure-target model or reconstruct capture and argument ABI from consumers.

Current proof

Production native lowering emits CallClosure and TailCallClosure with direct_target=None. build_codegen_closure_targets returns an empty map. Concrete direct executable calls and NativeCallableBoundaryId wrappers own the live direct and public paths respectively. The former closure-target registry and its direct-target branches are therefore unreachable alternate representations.

Work

fz-9i4.4.4 deletes NativeClosureTargetSurface, NativeCodegenSurface.closure_targets, build_codegen_closure_targets, test-only registry and rebinding mechanics, dead direct-target entry/signature/terminator branches, and stale tests and documentation. Preserve producer-owned callable construction members, public boundary wrappers, and concrete direct-call facts.

Acceptance

No native layer reconstructs a callable surface from FnId, consumer inputs, or sibling inventory. Representative captured, curried, divergent-caller, distinct-Enum, zero-capture, and resource-destructor closures pass interp, run, and build. Library tests and strict clippy pass.
title: Complete the callable-boundary cutover by deleting the retired native closure-target model
